name: p0-ip-only-pulp-timer-apb3
description: One PULP APB Timer target model, no CPU and no DMA: the host drives APB3 read/write transactions at declared window offsets, samples the device's real responses and its own APB3 trace, and observes the device interrupt output without consuming it. A light declared sequence loop repeats the list twice; the last two reads are declared fault transactions at a register offset the timer does not implement and at a window offset no timer decodes.

transactions.note: disable timer 0 so the count cannot advance while it is written
the device must return the word that was written to the disabled timer
prescaler 5 with the enable bit clear
compare value 8; writing the compare register resets the count
the count reaches the compare value inside these idle ticks and the device's own compare interrupt pulses
the count after the compare hit: a real word, not asserted to one exact value
disable again so the next loop starts from a known state
declared fault transaction: offset 0x0c is inside the timer window but is register index 3, which the PULP timer does not implement
declared fault transaction: the timer decodes only two 16-byte register blocks, so this offset selects no timer and the shared address decoder answers with a zero word and PREADY
